role: ask_/audit RAG only. Never stuffed into L1C/X1C/P1C/F1C extract prompts. Quote must still come from the note.

passages.cite: Kwan P et al. Definition of drug resistant epilepsy: consensus proposal by the ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Commission on Therapeutic Strategies. Epilepsia. 2010;51(6):1069-1077.
passages.text: ILAE 2010: drug-resistant epilepsy is failure of two tolerated, appropriately chosen and used antiseizure-medication schedules (monotherapy or combination) to achieve sustained seizure freedom. A trial that was not tolerated or not adequate does not count. ICD 'intractable' is a billing word, not this definition.

passages.cite: Fisher RS et al. Instruction manual for the ILAE 2017 operational classification of seizure types. Epilepsia. 2017;58(4):531-542.
passages.text: ILAE 2017: seizure type is classified by the first feature of the seizure, not by later evolution. Words such as 'followed by' or 'then' name spread, not onset. Do not relabel a sensory start as a motor seizure because a motor phase came later.

passages.cite: Scheffer IE et al. ILAE classification of the epilepsies: Position paper of the ILAE Commission for Classification and Terminology. Epilepsia. 2017;58(4):512-521.
passages.text: ILAE 2017 epilepsies: type is focal, generalized, combined focal and generalized, or unknown, from the seizure types that occur. A named syndrome is a further layer, not a replacement for copying the note's own words into the extract table.

passages.cite: Hirsch LJ et al. American Clinical Neurophysiology Society's Standardized Critical Care EEG Terminology. J Clin Neurophysiol. 2013;30(1):1-27. Update 2021.
passages.text: ACNS: LTM, cEEG, video-EEG and ICU EEG name EEG studies (long-term or continuous monitoring), not antiseizure drugs. A sentence that 'escalates to LTM' is planning a study. Do not treat LTM as a medication name.

passages.cite: Hirsch LJ et al. ACNS Standardized Critical Care EEG Terminology. 2013 and 2021 update.
passages.text: ACNS: LPDs, GPDs and BiPDs are EEG pattern names (lateralized / generalized / bilateral independent periodic discharges). SCORE maps those patterns after they are extracted. A clinic letter that says 'no LPDs' is negation, not a finding.
